metadata.title: New equidistribution estimates of Zhang type

nodes.name: Asymptotic notation
nodes.statement: Defines asymptotic shorthand: $X \ll Y$ or $X = O(Y)$ if $|X| \le CY$ for fixed $C$; $X \lessapprox Y$ if $X \le x^{o(1)} Y$; $X \sim Y$ if $Y \ll X \ll Y$. A quantity is of polynomial size if $n = O(x^{O(1)})$.

nodes.name: Discrepancy
nodes.statement: $\Delta(\alpha; a\,(q)) := \sum_{n = a\,(q)} \alpha(n) - \frac{1}{\phi(q)}\sum_{(n,q)=1}\alpha(n)$.

nodes.name: Multiple dense divisibility
nodes.statement: Recursive definition: every $n$ is $0$-tuply $y$-densely divisible; $n$ is $i$-tuply $y$-densely divisible if for every $j+k=i-1$ and $1 \le R \le yn$ there is a factorization $n=qr$ with $y^{-1}R \le r \le R$, $q$ being $j$-tuply and $r$ being $k$-tuply $y$-densely divisible. Set $\mathcal{D}^{(i)}(y)$ collects them.

nodes.name: Squarefree set $\mathcal{S}_I$ and product $P_I$
nodes.statement: For $I \subset \mathbb{R}$, $\mathcal{S}_I$ is the set of squarefree natural numbers with prime factors in $I$; if $I$ is bounded, $P_I = \prod_{p \in I} p$.

nodes.name: Coefficient sequence and Siegel-Walfisz property
nodes.statement: $\alpha\colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $|\alpha(n)| \ll \tau^{O(1)}(n) \log^{O(1)} x$. Located at scale $N$ if supported on $[cN, CN]$. Has the Siegel-Walfisz property if $|\Delta(\alpha \mathbf{1}_{(\cdot,r)=1}; a\,(q))| \ll \tau(qr)^{O(1)} N \log^{-A} x$ for all primitive $a\,(q)$.

nodes.name: Type I, II, III estimates
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Type}_{\mathrm{I}}^{(i)}[\varpi,\delta,\sigma]$, $\mathrm{Type}_{\mathrm{II}}^{(i)}[\varpi,\delta]$, $\mathrm{Type}_{\mathrm{III}}^{(i)}[\varpi,\delta,\sigma]$ assert bounds $\sum_{q \le Q,\, q \in \mathcal{D}^{(i)}_I(x^\delta)} |\Delta(\alpha \star \beta;\,a\,(q))| \ll x \log^{-A} x$ at distinct ranges of scales for the constituent coefficient sequences.

nodes.name: Purity of $\ell$-adic sheaf
nodes.statement: An $\ell$-adic sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathbb{P}^1_{\mathbb{F}_p}$ is generically pure of weight $i$ if for every $k/\mathbb{F}_p$ and every $x \in U_\mathcal{F}(k)$, the eigenvalues of $\mathrm{Fr}_{x,k}$ on $\mathcal{F}_{\bar\eta}$ have all Galois conjugates of complex absolute value $|k|^{i/2}$.

nodes.name: Admissible sheaf and trace function
nodes.statement: An admissible sheaf over $k$ is a middle-extension sheaf on $\mathbb{P}^1_k$ pointwise pure of weight $0$. An admissible trace function is the restriction of $t_\mathcal{F}$ to $k$ for some admissible sheaf.

nodes.name: Conductor of a sheaf
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{cond}(\mathcal{F}) := \mathrm{rk}(\mathcal{F}) + |(\mathbb{P}^1 - U_\mathcal{F})(\bar k)| + \sum_{x \in (\mathbb{P}^1 - U_\mathcal{F})(\bar k)} \mathrm{swan}_x(\mathcal{F})$.

nodes.name: Admissible Fourier sheaf
nodes.statement: An admissible sheaf is a Fourier sheaf if its geometrically irreducible components are neither trivial nor Artin-Schreier sheaves $\mathcal{L}_\psi$ for some non-trivial additive character $\psi$.

nodes.name: No polynomial phase
nodes.statement: An admissible sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ over $\mathbb{P}^1_k$ has no polynomial phase of degree $\le d$ if no geometrically irreducible component of $\mathcal{F}$ is geometrically isomorphic to $\mathcal{L}_{\psi(P(x))}$ with $P \in \mathbb{F}_p[X]$ of degree $\le d$.

nodes.name: Main theorem (equidistribution to smooth squarefree moduli)
nodes.statement: Let $\theta = 1/2 + 7/300$. For $\varepsilon > 0$, $A \ge 1$ fixed, and arbitrary primitive residues $a_p$ glued by CRT to $a_q$, there exists $\delta > 0$ such that $\sum_{q \le x^{\theta-\varepsilon},\, q\,x^\delta\text{-smooth squarefree}} |\psi(x;q,a_q) - \frac{x}{\varphi(q)}| \ll \frac{x}{(\log x)^A}$.
assumptions: $a_p$ is invertible mod $p$ for each prime $p$
$a_q$ is the CRT lift to squarefree $q$
conclusions: There exists $\delta = \delta(\varepsilon) > 0$ such that for $x \ge 1$, $\sum_{q \le x^{\theta-\varepsilon},\, q\,x^\delta\text{-smooth, squarefree}} |\psi(x;q,a_q) - x/\varphi(q)| \ll x/(\log x)^A$

nodes.name: Crude bounds on $\tau$
nodes.statement: For $d$ of polynomial size, $\tau(d) \lessapprox 1$; $\sum_{d \le y} \tau^C(d) \ll y \log^{O(1)} x$; and $\sum_{d \le y,\, d=a(q)} \tau^C(d) \ll \frac{y}{q}\tau^{O(1)}(q) \log^{O(1)} x + x^{o(1)}$.

nodes.name: Ramanujan averaging
nodes.statement: For integer $q \ge 1$ and $K \ge 1$, $\sum_{1 \le k \le K}(k,q) \le K\tau(q)$. Hence $\sum_{a \in \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}}(a,q) \lessapprox q$ for polynomial-size $q$, and $\sum_{|k| \le K}(k,q) \ll Kq^\varepsilon + q$ for any fixed $\varepsilon > 0$.

nodes.name: Modified Motohashi-Pintz-Zhang estimate $\mathrm{MPZ}^{(i)}[\varpi,\delta]$
nodes.statement: For bounded $I \subset \mathbb{R}$, $Q \lessapprox x^{1/2 + 2\varpi}$, integer $a$ coprime to $P_I$, and $A \ge 1$ fixed: $\sum_{q \le Q,\, q \in \mathcal{D}_I^{(i)}(x^\delta)} |\Delta(\Lambda \mathbf{1}_{[x,2x]}; a\,(q))| \ll x \log^{-A} x$.

nodes.name: Motohashi-Pintz-Zhang type estimates
nodes.statement: (i) $\mathrm{MPZ}^{(4)}[\varpi,\delta]$ holds whenever $600\varpi + 180\delta < 7$. (ii) $\mathrm{MPZ}^{(2)}[\varpi,\delta]$ holds whenever $168\varpi + 48\delta < 1$, without invoking Deligne's results.

nodes.name: Combinatorial lemma
nodes.statement: Let $i \ge 1$, $0 < \varpi < 1/4$, $0 < \delta < 1/4 + \varpi$, $1/10 < \sigma < 1/2$ with $\sigma > 2\varpi$. If $\mathrm{Type}_{\mathrm{I}}^{(i)}[\varpi,\delta,\sigma]$, $\mathrm{Type}_{\mathrm{II}}^{(i)}[\varpi,\delta]$ and $\mathrm{Type}_{\mathrm{III}}^{(i)}[\varpi,\delta,\sigma]$ all hold, then $\mathrm{MPZ}^{(i)}[\varpi,\delta]$ holds. If additionally $\sigma > 1/6$, the Type III hypothesis can be dropped.

nodes.name: New Type I, II, III estimates
nodes.statement: (i) $54\varpi + 15\delta + 5\sigma < 1 \Rightarrow \mathrm{Type}_{\mathrm{I}}^{(1)}[\varpi,\delta,\sigma]$. (ii) $56\varpi + 16\delta + 4\sigma < 1 \Rightarrow \mathrm{Type}_{\mathrm{I}}^{(2)}[\varpi,\delta,\sigma]$. (iii) $\frac{160}{3}\varpi + 16\delta + \frac{34}{9}\sigma < 1$ and $64\varpi + 18\delta + 2\sigma < 1$ $\Rightarrow \mathrm{Type}_{\mathrm{I}}^{(4)}[\varpi,\delta,\sigma]$. (iv) $68\varpi + 14\delta < 1 \Rightarrow \mathrm{Type}_{\mathrm{II}}^{(1)}[\varpi,\delta]$. (v) $\sigma > 1/18 + (28/9)\varpi + (2/9)\delta$ and $\varpi < 1/12 \Rightarrow \mathrm{Type}_{\mathrm{III}}^{(1)}[\varpi,\delta,\sigma]$.
conclusions: Implications producing $\mathrm{Type}_{\mathrm{I}}^{(1)}, \mathrm{Type}_{\mathrm{I}}^{(2)}, \mathrm{Type}_{\mathrm{I}}^{(4)}, \mathrm{Type}_{\mathrm{II}}^{(1)}, \mathrm{Type}_{\mathrm{III}}^{(1)}$ under stated linear inequalities

nodes.name: Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem (bilinear form)
nodes.statement: For $NM \sim x$, $N \ge x^\varepsilon$, and coefficient sequences $\alpha,\beta$ at scales $M,N$ with $\beta$ Siegel-Walfisz, there is $B = B(A)$ with $\sum_{q \le x^{1/2}\log^{-B}x}\sup_{a \in (\mathbb{Z}/q)^\times}|\Delta(\alpha \star \beta;\,a\,(q))| \ll x \log^{-A} x$.

nodes.name: Properties of dense divisibility
nodes.statement: (0) Monotonicity in $y$ and $i$. (i) If $n$ is $i$-tuply $y$-densely divisible and $m \mid n$, then $m$ is $i$-tuply $y(n/m)$-densely divisible; similarly for multiples. (ii) If $m,n$ are $y$-densely divisible, so is $[m,n]$. (iii) Any $y$-smooth number is $i$-tuply $y$-densely divisible. (iv) Sufficient prime-product condition.
conclusions: Monotonicity, divisor/multiple inheritance, lcm closure, smoothness implies dense divisibility, and sufficient condition (iv)

nodes.name: Combinatorial trichotomy on partition sums
nodes.statement: If $1/10 < \sigma < 1/2$ and $t_1+\cdots+t_n=1$ with $t_i \ge 0$, at least one of the alternatives holds: (Type 0) some $t_i \ge 1/2 + \sigma$; (Type I/II) a partition $\{1,\ldots,n\} = S \cup T$ with $1/2-\sigma < \sum_S t_i \le \sum_T t_i < 1/2 + \sigma$; (Type III) distinct $i,j,k$ with $2\sigma \le t_i \le t_j \le t_k \le 1/2-\sigma$ and pairwise sums $\ge 1/2+\sigma$. If $\sigma > 1/6$, Type III cannot occur.
conclusions: At least one of (Type 0), (Type I/II), (Type III) holds

nodes.name: Heath-Brown identity
nodes.statement: For any $K \ge 1$, $\Lambda = \sum_{j=1}^K (-1)^{j-1}\binom{K}{j}\mu_{\le}^{\star j} \star \mathbf{1}^{\star(j-1)} \star L$ on $[x,2x]$, where $\mu_{\le}(n) = \mu(n)\mathbf{1}_{n \le (2x)^{1/K}}$.
conclusions: Identity decomposing $\Lambda$ on $[x,2x]$ into Dirichlet convolutions

nodes.name: Properties of the convolved coefficient functions $\alpha_k$
nodes.statement: Each $\alpha_k$ from the Heath-Brown decomposition is a coefficient sequence at scale $N_k$; if $N_k \gg x^{2\sigma}$ then $\alpha_k$ is smooth; if $N_k \gg x^\varepsilon$ then $\alpha_k$ has the Siegel-Walfisz property; and $N_1 \cdots N_{2j} \sim x$.
assumptions: Notation as in the Heath-Brown decomposition
conclusions: $\alpha_S$ is a coefficient sequence at scale $\prod_{k \in S} N_k$

nodes.name: One-variable exponential sums with additive characters (Weil)
nodes.statement: For $P,Q \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ and a prime $p$ with $Q\,(p) \ne 0$ and $P/Q\,(p) \ne g^p - g + c$ in $\mathbb{F}_p(X)$, we have $|\sum_{x \in \mathbb{F}_p} e_p(P(x)/Q(x))| \ll \sqrt{p}$ with implied constant linear in $\max(\deg P, \deg Q)$.
nodes.origin_citation: Weil (Riemann hypothesis for curves); Perelmuter; Bombieri-Stepanov

nodes.name: Chinese Remainder Theorem for $e_q$
nodes.statement: If $q_1,q_2$ are coprime, then $e_{q_1q_2}(a) = e_{q_1}(a/q_2)\,e_{q_2}(a/q_1)$ for any $a \in \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{Q})$. Generalizes by induction to $k$ pairwise coprime moduli.

nodes.name: Fundamental theorem of calculus for rational functions mod $q$
nodes.statement: For $f = P/Q \in \mathbb{Q}(X)$ with $Q\,(p) \ne 0$ for $p \mid q$ and large enough prime factors: (i) $q \mid f' \Rightarrow$ there is $c$ with $q \mid f - c$. (ii) For squarefree $q$ with $\deg(P) < \deg(Q)$, $(q,f') \mid (q,f)$.

nodes.name: Ramanujan-Weil bounds
nodes.statement: For squarefree $q$ and $f = P/Q \in \mathbb{Q}(X)$ with $Q$ non-zero mod each $p \mid q$, $|\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}} e_q(f(n))| \le C^{\Omega(q)} q^{1/2}\frac{(f',q)}{(f'',q)^{1/2}}$ for some $C \ge 1$ depending on $\deg(P), \deg(Q)$.

nodes.name: Two-modulus exponential sum bound
nodes.statement: For squarefree $d_1,d_2$ and integers $c_1,c_2,l_1,l_2$, $|\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}/[d_1,d_2]\mathbb{Z}} e_{d_1}(c_1/(n+l_1))\,e_{d_2}(c_2/(n+l_2))| \le C^{\Omega([d_1,d_2])}(c_1,\delta_1)(c_2,\delta_2)(d_1,d_2)$ where $\delta_i = d_i/(d_1,d_2)$.
conclusions: Stated bound on the two-character mixed sum

nodes.name: Completion of sums (Polya-Vinogradov)
nodes.statement: For $\psi_M(x) = \psi((x-x_0)/M)$ smooth at scale $M$ and integer $q \ge 1$: $|\sum_m \psi_M(m) f(m) - (M'/q)\sum_{m \in \mathbb{Z}/q} f(m)| \ll q^{1/2}\log^{O(1)}M\,\sup_{h \ne 0}|\widehat{f}_q(h)|$, with refined variants summing over $|h| \le qM^{-1+\varepsilon}$.
assumptions: $\psi$ smooth supported on $[c,C]$, derivatives controlled by $\log^{O(1)}M$
conclusions: Polya-Vinogradov type bound and a frequency-restricted refinement (eq. complete-1, complete-1b, complete-3)

nodes.name: Incomplete additive character sums
nodes.statement: For $f = P/Q \in \mathbb{Q}(X)$ with $\deg P < \deg Q$ and squarefree $q = rs$, smooth weights $\psi_N$ at scale $N$: $|\sum_n \psi_N(n) e_q(f(n))| \ll q^\varepsilon(q^{1/2} + (N/q)|\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}/q}e_q(f(n))|)$, and using one $q$-van der Corput step: $|\sum_n \psi_N(n) e_q(f(n))| \ll q^\varepsilon(N^{1/2}r^{1/2} + N^{1/2}s^{1/4} + \dots)$.
assumptions: $q$ squarefree, $f = P/Q$ with $\deg P < \deg Q$, $N \ll q^{O(1)}$

nodes.name: Incomplete two-character sums under dense divisibility (Corollary `dons')
nodes.statement: For squarefree $d_1,d_2$ with $[d_1,d_2]$ being $y$-densely divisible, divisor $d \mid [d_1,d_2]$, and residue class $a\,(d)$, $|\sum_{n=a(d)} \psi_N(n) e_{d_1}(c_1/(n+l_1))\,e_{d_2}(c_2/(n+l_2))| \ll [d_1,d_2]^\varepsilon (d^{-1/2}N^{1/2}[d_1,d_2]^{1/6}y^{1/6} + d^{-1}\frac{(c_1,\delta'_1)}{\delta'_1}\frac{(c_2,\delta'_2)}{\delta'_2}N)$.
conclusions: Stated incomplete-sum bound under dense divisibility, plus a non-vdC variant

nodes.name: New Type I and Type II estimates (restatement)
nodes.statement: Reformulation of TP395.3 cases (i)-(iv) in the explicit form $\sum_{d \in \mathcal{D}_I^{(i)}(x^\delta),\, d \lessapprox x^{1/2+2\varpi}}|\Delta(\alpha \star \beta;\,a\,(d))| \ll x \log^{-A}x$ under the four hypothesis sets distinguishing Type I and Type II ranges.
conclusions: Bound $\sum_{d \lessapprox x^{1/2+2\varpi}}|\Delta(\alpha \star \beta;\,a\,(d))| \ll x \log^{-A}x$ under the four hypothesis sets (typeI1, typeI2, typeI4, typeII1)

nodes.name: Few moduli with many small prime factors (lemma roar)
nodes.statement: For $D_0 = \exp(\log^{1/3} x)$ and $\mathcal{E}(D)$ the set of $d \in [D,2D]$ with $\prod_{p \mid d, p \le D_0} p > \exp(\log^{2/3} x)$, we have $|\mathcal{E}(D)| \ll D \log^{-A} x$ for any fixed $A > 0$.

nodes.name: Exponential sum estimates for Type I/II reductions (Theorem `eset')
nodes.statement: Reduction of Theorems TP395.3-TP395.5 to bounds $\sum_r \Upsilon_{\ell,r}(b_1,b_2;q_0) \lessapprox x^{-\varepsilon} Q^2 R N (q_0,\ell)q_0^{-2}$ for the phase-function-weighted sums $\Upsilon_{\ell,r}$, under the hypothesis sets (typeI1, typeI2, typeI4, typeII1).

nodes.name: Exponential sum bound for Type II reduction (Proposition `exse')
nodes.statement: For $\mathbf{p} = (h_1,h_2,q_1,q_2,s_1,s_2)$ with the appropriate coprimality and $\ell \ne 0$, $|S_{\ell,r}(\mathbf{p})| \lessapprox (q_0,\ell)\big(q_0^{-2}Q^2 R^{1/2} + (N/(q_0R))(h_1 s_1 s_2 - h_2 q_1 q_2, r)\big)$.

nodes.name: Exponential sum bound for first Type I (Proposition `exse-2')
nodes.statement: For appropriate $\mathbf{p} = (h_1,h_2,q_1,q_2,q_1,s_2)$ with $q_0 q_i r, q_0 s_2 r \in \mathcal{D}_I(x^\delta)$, $|S_{\ell,r}(\mathbf{p})| \lessapprox q_0^{1/6}N^{1/2}x^{\delta/6}(Q^3R)^{1/6} + R^{-1}N(h_1 s_2 - h_2 q_2, r)$.
assumptions: $q_0 q_i r, q_0 s_2 r$ are $x^\delta$-densely divisible
conclusions: Stated bound for $|S_{\ell,r}|$ in the first Type I setting

nodes.name: Exponential sum bound for second Type I (Proposition `exse-3')
nodes.statement: For $\mathbf{p} = (h_1,h_2,u_1,v_1,v_2,q_2,q_0)$ with the displayed coprimality, $|T_{\ell,r}(\mathbf{p})| \lessapprox (q_0,\ell)\big(q_0^{-1/2}N^{1/2}x^{\delta/3+\varepsilon/3}(RHQ^2)^{1/6} + N(h_1 v_2 - h_2 v_1, r)/(q_0 R)\big)$.

nodes.name: Sums of trace functions (Deligne)
nodes.statement: For an admissible sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathbb{P}^1_k$ with $|k|=q$ and $U=U_\mathcal{F}$, $S(\mathcal{F};k) = q\,\mathrm{Tr}(\mathrm{Fr}_k \mid (\mathcal{F}_{\bar\eta})_{\pi_1^g(U)}) + O(\mathrm{cond}(\mathcal{F})^2 q^{1/2})$.

nodes.name: Square-root cancellation for correlations
nodes.statement: For admissible $\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}$ on $\mathbb{P}^1_k$ with no common irreducible constituent, $|C(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G};k)| \ll (\mathrm{cond}(\mathcal{F})\mathrm{cond}(\mathcal{G}))^4 q^{1/2}$. If both conductors are bounded, $|C(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G};k)| \ll q^{1/2}$.
assumptions: $\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G}$ admissible with no common irreducible constituent

nodes.name: Sheaf-theoretic Fourier transform
nodes.statement: For admissible Fourier sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathbb{P}^1_k$ and non-trivial $\psi$, there is an admissible Fourier sheaf $\mathcal{G} = \mathrm{FT}_\psi(\mathcal{F})$ such that $t_\mathcal{G}(\cdot;k') = \mathrm{FT}_{\psi_{k'}}t_\mathcal{F}(\cdot;k)$. The transform is essentially involutive (eq-fourier-inv) and $\mathrm{cond}(\mathcal{G}) \le 10\,\mathrm{cond}(\mathcal{F})^2$.
nodes.origin_citation: Deligne; Laumon; Katz GKM Chapter 8; FKM1

nodes.name: Hyper-Kloosterman sheaf (Deligne-Katz)
nodes.statement: For $m \ge 1$ and odd $p$, there is an admissible Fourier sheaf $\mathcal{K}\ell_m$ with $t_{\mathcal{K}\ell_m}(x;k) = (-1)^{m-1}\mathrm{Kl}_m(x;k)$ for $x \in k^\times$. It is lisse on $\mathbb{G}_m$, of rank $m$, geometrically irreducible, with monodromy $\mathrm{SL}_m$ ($m$ odd) or $\mathrm{Sp}_m$ ($m$ even); $\mathrm{cond}(\mathcal{K}\ell_m) = m+3$ for $m \ge 2$.
conclusions: Existence of $\mathcal{K}\ell_m$ with the listed sheaf-theoretic properties

nodes.name: Estimates for hyper-Kloosterman sums
nodes.statement: For $m \ge 2$ and additive character $\psi'$, $|\sum_{x \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times} \mathrm{Kl}_m(x;p)\psi'(x)| \ll p^{1/2}$. For $a \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times$ with $a \ne 1$ or $\psi' \ne 1$, $|\sum_{x \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times} \mathrm{Kl}_m(x;p)\overline{\mathrm{Kl}_m(ax;p)}\psi'(x)| \ll p^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: No-polynomial-phase invariance theorem (Theorem `th-pol-phase')
nodes.statement: For prime $p > d$ and isotypic admissible $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathbb{P}^1_{\mathbb{F}_p}$ with no polynomial phase of degree $\le d$: either $\mathrm{cond}(\mathcal{F}) \ge p+1$, or for any $l \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times$, $\mathcal{F} \otimes [+l]^*\check{\mathcal{F}}$ has no polynomial phase of degree $\le d-1$. In all cases, $|\sum_{x \in \mathbb{F}_p} t_\mathcal{F}(x+l)\overline{t_\mathcal{F}(x)}\psi(P(x))| \ll p^{1/2}$ for $l \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times$ and $P$ of degree $d-1$, with implied constant polynomial in $\mathrm{cond}(\mathcal{F})$ and $d$.
assumptions: $\mathcal{F}$ isotypic admissible with no polynomial phase $\le d$
conclusions: Either $\mathrm{cond}(\mathcal{F}) \ge p+1$ or $[+l]^*\check{\mathcal{F}} \otimes \mathcal{F}$ has no polynomial phase $\le d-1$

nodes.name: Trace function bound for two-pole rational phases (Theorem `kf-bound')
nodes.statement: For $(a,b,c,d,e) \in \mathbb{F}_p^5$ with $a \ne c$ and $f(X,Y) = \frac{1}{(Y+aX+b)(Y+cX+d)} + eY$, the function $x \mapsto K_f(x;p)$ is the trace function of an admissible geometrically irreducible sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ with conductor $O(1)$ and no polynomial phase of degree $\le 2$. Hence $|\sum_x K_f(x;p)\psi(hx)| \ll p^{1/2}$ and the Weyl-shift bound holds for $(h,l) \ne (0,0)$.
conclusions: $K_f$ is the trace function of an admissible geometrically irreducible sheaf with bounded conductor
$\mathcal{F}$ has no polynomial phase of degree $\le 2$

nodes.name: Incomplete sum of trace function (van der Corput)
nodes.statement: For squarefree $q$ of polynomial size, admissible trace function $t(\cdot;q)$ from sheaves $(\mathcal{F}_p)_{p \mid q}$, and smooth $\psi_N$: (i) if no $\mathcal{F}_p$ has polynomial phase $\le 1$, $|\sum_n \psi_N(n) t(n;q)| \ll q^{1/2+\varepsilon}(1 + N/q)$. (ii) if no $\mathcal{F}_p$ has polynomial phase $\le 2$, then for any $q = rs$ and $N \le q$: $|\sum_n \psi_N(n) t(n;q)| \ll q^\varepsilon (N^{1/2} r^{1/2} + N^{1/2} s^{1/4})$.
conclusions: (i) Polya-Vinogradov + Deligne bound when no degree-$\le 1$ polynomial phase
(ii) van der Corput + Deligne bound when no degree-$\le 2$ polynomial phase

nodes.name: Specialized vdC bound for the rational kernel $K(x;q)$ (Corollary `inctrace-q')
nodes.statement: For squarefree $q$ and $K(x;q) = q^{-1/2}\sum_y e_q(f(x,y))$ with $f(x,y) = 1/((y+ax+b)(y+cx+d)) + ey$ and $(a-c,q) = 1$: $|\sum_n \psi_N(n) K(n;q)| \ll q^{1/2+\varepsilon}(1 + N/q)$, and for any $q = rs$ with $N \le q$, $|\sum_n \psi_N(n) K(n;q)| \ll q^\varepsilon (N^{1/2}r^{1/2} + N^{1/2}s^{1/4})$.
conclusions: Polya-Vinogradov + Deligne bound, plus the vdC refinement

nodes.name: Correlation of hyper-Kloosterman sums (Lemma `lm-c-kl')
nodes.statement: For squarefree $s,r_1,r_2$ with $(s,r_1) = (s,r_2) = 1$, and $a_1 \in (\mathbb{Z}/r_1 s)^\times, a_2 \in (\mathbb{Z}/r_2 s)^\times$: $|\sum_{h \in (\mathbb{Z}/s[r_1,r_2])^\times} \mathrm{Kl}_3(a_1 h;r_1 s)\overline{\mathrm{Kl}_3(a_2 h;r_2 s)} e_{[r_1,r_2]s}(nh)| \ll (s[r_1,r_2])^\varepsilon s^{1/2}[r_1,r_2]^{1/2}(a_2-a_1,n,r_1,r_2)^{1/2}(a_2 r_1^3 - a_1 r_2^3,n,s)^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Correlation of hyper-Kloosterman sums II (Corollary `corr-2')
nodes.statement: Smooth-weight version: $|\sum_{(h,s[r_1,r_2])=1} \Psi_H(h)\mathrm{Kl}_3(a_1 h;r_1 s)\overline{\mathrm{Kl}_3(a_2 h;r_2 s)}| \ll (s[r_1,r_2])^\varepsilon (H/[r_1,r_2]s + 1) s^{1/2}[r_1,r_2]^{1/2}(a_2-a_1,r_1,r_2)^{1/2}(a_2 r_1^3 - a_1 r_2^3,s)^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Katz Sato-Tate equidistribution law
nodes.statement: As $p \to \infty$, the angles $\{\theta(n;p): 1 \le n \le p\}$ become equidistributed in $[0,\pi]$ with respect to the Sato-Tate measure $d\mu_{ST}(\theta) = \frac{2}{\pi}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta$.
conclusions: Equidistribution of Kloosterman angles with respect to $\mu_{ST}$

nodes.name: Sato-Tate over short ranges for composite moduli
nodes.statement: For $q = rs$, $r,s$ distinct primes with $s^{1/2} \le r \le 2 s^{1/2}$, and any $\varepsilon > 0$, the pairs $(\theta(n\bar s^2;r),\theta(n\bar r^2;s))$ for $1 \le n \le q^{1/3+\varepsilon}$ become equidistributed in $[0,\pi]^2$ with respect to $\mu_{ST} \times \mu_{ST}$ as $q \to \infty$. Consequently the angles $\theta(n;q)$ equidistribute on $[0,\pi]$ with respect to a pushforward measure $\mu_{ST,2}$.
conclusions: Equidistribution of pair-angles in $[0,\pi]^2$ with respect to $\mu_{ST} \times \mu_{ST}$ over $1 \le n \le q^{1/3+\varepsilon}$
Pushforward equidistribution of $\theta(n;q)$ with respect to $\mu_{ST,2}$

nodes.name: New Type III estimates
nodes.statement: Under $MN_1 N_2 N_3 \sim x$, $N_1 N_2, N_1 N_3, N_2 N_3 \gtrapprox x^{1/2+\sigma}$, $x^{2\sigma} \lessapprox N_i \lessapprox x^{1/2-\sigma}$, smooth $\psi_i$ at scales $N_i$: $\sum_{d \in \mathcal{D}_I(x^\delta),\,d \lessapprox x^{1/2+2\varpi}} |\Delta(\alpha \star \psi_1 \star \psi_2 \star \psi_3;\,a\,(d))| \ll x \log^{-A}x$, provided $\varpi < 1/12$ and $\sigma > 1/18 + (28/9)\varpi + (2/9)\delta$.
assumptions: $N_1 N_2, N_1 N_3, N_2 N_3 \gtrapprox x^{1/2+\sigma}$

nodes.name: Diagonal/off-diagonal collection in Type III (Lemma `lm-sumup')
nodes.statement: $T''_2 \lessapprox (M^2 Q^2/b^2)\big(\frac{H_{\mathbf{b}} b^{1/2}}{Q^{1/2}}(bS/Q)^{1/2} + \frac{Q^{1/2}}{b^{1/2}}(x^\delta Q/S)^{1/2}\big)$, summing the off-diagonal contribution from the Cauchy-Schwarz expansion in the Type III estimate.
assumptions: Notation as in the Type III reduction
conclusions: Stated bound on the off-diagonal sum $T''_2$

nodes.name: Convergent radical-weighted Euler series (Lemma `lm-euler')
nodes.statement: The series $\sum_{b_1,b_2,b_3 \ge 1}\frac{b_1^\flat b_2^\flat b_3^\flat}{(b_1 b_2 b_3)^{1/2} b^3}$ converges, where $b = (b_1 b_2 b_3)^\flat$ and $n^\flat$ is the squarefree radical.

nodes.name: Bound on $\Upsilon_4$ for the improved Type I (Proposition `pr-upsilon-4')
nodes.statement: $\Upsilon_4(h_1,v_1,h_2,v_2) \lessapprox (q_0,\ell)\,x^{-2\varepsilon}\,\Delta\,N\,H^{-2}\,q_0\,(h_1 v_2 - h_2 v_1, q_0 q_2 r_1 u_1 [v_1,v_2])$, taking $D = x^{-5\varepsilon} N/H^4$, under the conditions $\frac{160}{3}\varpi + 16\delta + \frac{34}{9}\sigma < 1$ and $64\varpi + 18\delta + 2\sigma < 1$.
assumptions: Notation as in the improved Type I reduction
conclusions: $\Upsilon_4 \lessapprox (q_0,\ell) x^{-2\varepsilon}\Delta N H^{-2} q_0 (h_1 v_2 - h_2 v_1, q_0 q_2 r_1 u_1 [v_1,v_2])$

nodes.name: GCD sum over $(h_1,v_1,h_2,v_2)$ (Lemma `lm-gcd')
assumptions: Notation as in the improved Type I reduction

nodes.name: Auxiliary clean-up identity for $\Psi(d,n+dl)$ (Lemma `lm-clean-up')
nodes.statement: Let $m = q_0 r_1 u_1 [v_1,v_2] q_2$. There exist residue classes $\alpha\,(m), \beta\,(m)$, independent of $n,l$, such that $\Psi(d,n+dl) = \xi(n,d) e_m(\alpha/[d(n+(\beta+l)d)])$ with $|\xi(n,d)| \le 1$ and $(\alpha,m) = (h_1 v_2 - h_2 v_1, m)$.
assumptions: Notation as in the improved Type I reduction
conclusions: Stated factorization with $(\alpha,m) = (h_1 v_2 - h_2 v_1, m)$

nodes.name: Two-variable van der Corput bound (Proposition `lode')
nodes.statement: For squarefree $y$-densely divisible $m$ of polynomial size and $\alpha,\beta,\gamma_1,\gamma_2,l \in \mathbb{Z}/m$: $|\sum_d \sum_n \psi_\Delta(d)\psi'_N(n) e_m(\alpha l/[(n+\beta d+\gamma_1)(n+(\beta+l)d+\gamma_2)])| \lessapprox (\alpha l, m)(N/(q_0 m^{1/2}) + m^{1/2})(1 + (\Delta/q_0)^{1/2} m^{1/6} y^{1/6} + (\Delta/q_0) m^{-1/2})$, with a parallel non-vdC bound substituting $m^{1/2}$ for the parenthesized vdC factor.

nodes.name: Convention for $e_q(P/Q)$ at vanishing denominators
nodes.statement: For $P=X$, $Q=X+3$, $q=3$: although $P\,(q)$ and $Q\,(q)$ both vanish at $x=0$, by the convention via $\mathbb{P}^1$, $e_q(f(0)) = 1$.

nodes.name: Ramanujan and Kloosterman sums via Ramanujan-Weil
nodes.statement: (1) $f(X) = b/X$ recovers a slightly weaker Ramanujan sum bound $|\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}/q} e_q(bn)\mathbf{1}_{(n,q)=1}| \le (b,q)$. (2) $f = a/X + bX$ recovers the Kloosterman bound $|\sum_n e_q(a\bar n + bn)\mathbf{1}_{(n,q)=1}| \le 2^{\Omega(q)}q^{1/2}(a,b,q)/(a,q)^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma `sum' (combinatorial trichotomy)
nodes.statement: Assume Type 0 and Type I/II fail; deduce Type III by the powerful/powerless element analysis. The constraint $\sigma > 1/10$ ensures every pair of `powerful' elements yields a large set; this prevents 4 powerful elements, leaving exactly 3.

nodes.name: Dispose of $\sigma > 1/6$ corner case
nodes.statement: If $\sigma > 1/6$ then $2\sigma > 1/2 - \sigma$, so the inequalities $2\sigma \le t_i \le t_j \le t_k \le 1/2 - \sigma$ of Type III are inconsistent; Type III cannot occur.

nodes.name: Set up: assume Type 0 and Type I/II fail
nodes.statement: Assume failure of Type 0 ($t_i < 1/2 + \sigma$ for all $i$) and Type I/II ($\sum_{i \in S} t_i \notin (1/2 - \sigma, 1/2 + \sigma)$). Define `large' / `small' subsets accordingly.

nodes.name: Powerless elements are absorbed
nodes.statement: An element $i$ is powerful if some small set $S$ becomes large by adding $i$; otherwise powerless. Adding/removing powerless elements from a set preserves smallness/largeness; the union of a small set with a set of powerless elements is small.

nodes.name: Exactly three powerful elements
nodes.statement: There are at least two powerful elements (complement of the small `powerless' set is large with $\ge 2$ elements). Picking one yields a large complement with $\ge 2$ more, giving at least three. The bound $\sigma > 1/10$ rules out four powerful elements via $1 \ge 2(1/2 + \sigma) > 1$.

nodes.name: Conclude Type III holds
nodes.statement: Order the three powerful elements $t_i \le t_j \le t_k$; powerful $\Rightarrow t_\bullet \ge 2\sigma$, and pairs $\{i,j\},\{i,k\},\{j,k\}$ are large by powerful-pair argument, giving $t_i+t_j, t_i+t_k, t_j+t_k \ge 1/2 + \sigma$.

nodes.name: Proof of the Heath-Brown identity (Lemma LP395.6)
nodes.statement: Decompose $\mu = \mu_{\le} + \mu_>$ and use the binomial theorem on $\mu_>^{\star K} \star \mathbf{1}^{\star K-1} \star L$ which vanishes on $[1,2x]$. The $j=0$ term equals $\Lambda$ via $\mu \star L = \Lambda$; other terms simplify by $\mu \star \mathbf{1} = \delta$.

nodes.name: Decompose Mobius and expand
nodes.statement: Write $\mu = \mu_{\le} + \mu_>$ where $\mu_>(n) = \mu(n)\mathbf{1}_{n > (2x)^{1/K}}$. Expand $\mu_>^{\star K}$ via binomial formula.

nodes.name: Vanishing on $[1,2x]$
nodes.statement: Note $\mu_>^{\star K} \star \mathbf{1}^{\star K-1} \star L$ vanishes on $[1,2x]$ since the product of $K$ factors all $> (2x)^{1/K}$ exceeds $2x$.

nodes.name: Identify the $j=0$ term as $\Lambda$
nodes.statement: Using $\mu \star L = \Lambda$ and $\mu \star \mathbf{1} = \delta$, the $j=0$ term reduces to $\Lambda$.

nodes.name: Simplify the remaining terms
nodes.statement: For $j \ge 1$, repeated use of $\mu \star \mathbf{1} = \delta$ collapses $\mu^{\star (K-j)} \star \mu_{\le}^{\star j} \star \mathbf{1}^{\star K-1} \star L$ into $\mu_{\le}^{\star j} \star \mathbf{1}^{\star (j-1)} \star L$, yielding the claimed identity.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma LP395.3 (Combinatorial lemma) via Heath-Brown + Lemma LP395.5
nodes.statement: Reduce $\mathrm{MPZ}^{(i)}$ to (sss) via Heath-Brown; further reduce to (tap) via finer-than-dyadic decomposition. Apply LP395.5 to the exponents $t_k$ to split into Type 0, Type I/II, Type III cases. Use Definitions DP395.5 / DP395.6 to identify each case as a Type I/II/III hypothesis or as a smooth-large-scale `Type 0' computation.

nodes.name: Heath-Brown reduction with $K$ chosen so $1/K < 2\sigma$
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma LP395.6 with $K$ such that $1/K < 2\sigma$. By the triangle inequality reduce $\mathrm{MPZ}^{(i)}$ to bounding the $j$-fold convolution piece for each $1 \le j \le K$.

nodes.name: Finer-than-dyadic decomposition
nodes.statement: Insert smooth partition of unity $\sum_{N \in \mathcal{D}} \psi_N(n) = 1$ with $\Theta = 1 + \log^{-A_0} x$. Reduce to the bound (tap) for products of weighted convolutions $\alpha_{S} \star \alpha_{T}$.

nodes.name: Apply combinatorial trichotomy
nodes.statement: Set $N_k \sim x^{t_k}$ with $\sum t_k = 1$ (LP395.7 (iv)) and apply LP395.5: one of (Type 0)/(Type I/II)/(Type III) holds.

nodes.name: Type I/II case
nodes.statement: Partition $\{1,\ldots,2j\} = S \cup T$. Both $\alpha_S, \alpha_T$ are coefficient sequences with the Siegel-Walfisz property. Definition DP395.6 applies and the result follows from the Type I or Type II hypothesis depending on $N_S$.

nodes.name: Type III case
nodes.statement: Identify the three large $\alpha_k$'s as the smooth $\psi_1,\psi_2,\psi_3$ in DP395.6 (iii); the Type III hypothesis directly gives the bound.

nodes.name: Type 0 case (single large smooth factor)
nodes.statement: If some $t_k \ge 1/2 + \sigma$, then $\alpha_k$ is smooth at large scale (LP395.7 (ii)) and well-distributed via Poisson summation (essentially the Bombieri-Vinogradov range), giving the bound directly.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem TP395.10 (`kf-bound') via Fourier transform identification with $\mathrm{Kl}_3$
nodes.statement: Normalize parameters via Remark `invarianceremark' to reduce to $f = 1/((y+x)y) + ey$. Compute the Fourier transform of $K_f$ and identify it with $\mathrm{Kl}_3(z(e-z);p)$ on a dense open set. By Proposition PrP395.6 (Kloosterman sheaf properties) and the Fourier inversion (TP395.8), $K_f$ is the trace function of an admissible geometrically irreducible sheaf with bounded conductor. The no-polynomial-phase property follows from the same identification using Remark `invarianceremark'.

nodes.name: Reduce to canonical parameters
nodes.statement: By translation/dilation invariance reduce to $f(X,Y) = 1/((Y+X)Y) + eY$, equivalently the case $(a,b,c,d) = (1,0,0,0)$.

nodes.name: Compute the Fourier transform
nodes.statement: The change of variables $y_1 = 1/((y+x)y), y_2 = z(y+x)$ identifies the Fourier transform of $K_f$ with the hyper-Kloosterman sum $\mathrm{Kl}_3(z(e-z);p)$ for $z(e-z) \ne 0$.

nodes.name: Identify with Kloosterman sheaf via PrP395.6
nodes.statement: The map $z \mapsto z(e-z)$ pulls back $\mathcal{K}\ell_3$ to a sheaf with bounded conductor and irreducibility/no-polynomial-phase properties (using Remark `irrednopolynomialphase').

nodes.name: Apply Fourier inversion
nodes.statement: By the inversion formula (TP395.8) and the Fourier-invariance of `no polynomial phase of degree $\le 2$' (Remark `invarianceremark'), $K_f$ itself is admissible irreducible with bounded conductor and no polynomial phase of degree $\le 2$. Then $|\sum_x K_f(x;p)\psi(hx)| \ll p^{1/2}$ and the Weyl-shift bound follow from TP395.9.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem TP395.13 (Type III) via Cauchy-Schwarz + Corollary `corr-2'
nodes.statement: After Heath-Brown identity reduction (already done at the level of TP395.3) and CRT/coprime-set splitting on the convolution $\psi_1 \star \psi_2 \star \psi_3$, complete the inner sum using Lemma `com' to get hyper-Kloosterman sums $\mathrm{Kl}_3(\cdot;d)$. Use dense divisibility to factor $d = rs$ with $R, S \approx x^{1/4}$, apply Cauchy-Schwarz and bound diagonal/off-diagonal contributions via Corollary CP395.4; optimize the parameter $S$ to derive the linear inequality $\sigma > 1/18 + (28/9)\varpi + (2/9)\delta$.

nodes.name: Completion of sums and identification with Kl_3
nodes.statement: Expand the convolution and complete the sums (Lemma LP395.12) to express the inner triple sum as $q\,\mathrm{Kl}_3(a h_1 h_2 h_3;q)$.

nodes.name: Reduction to $T(\mathbf{b})$ after collecting common values
nodes.statement: Collect common values of $\ell = l_1 l_2 l_3$ to bound $|\Sigma_2'(Q;a)| \ll (Q/H)\sum_{\mathbf{b}} (b_1^\flat b_2^\flat b_3^\flat / b^2) T(\mathbf{b})$.

nodes.name: Factor $d=rs$ via dense divisibility
nodes.statement: Use the dense divisibility hypothesis to factor each $d \in \mathcal{D}_I(x^\delta)$ as $d = rs$ with $r, s$ in well-chosen ranges; this enables the Cauchy-Schwarz balancing.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz and bound diagonal $T'_2$
nodes.statement: Apply Cauchy-Schwarz to $T(\mathbf{b})$ and bound the diagonal contribution $T'_2 \lessapprox H_{\mathbf{b}} M Q S / b$ using Deligne's bound $|\mathrm{Kl}_3(x;d)| \lessapprox 1$.

nodes.name: Off-diagonal bound via Corollary `corr-2'
nodes.statement: For $m_1 r_1^3 \ne m_2 r_2^3$, apply Corollary CP395.4 to $U(r_1,r_2,s,m_1,m_2)$, then sum via Lemma LP395.15 to obtain the explicit upper bound on $T''_2$.

nodes.name: Optimize $S$ and conclude the parameter inequality
nodes.statement: Choose $S = \min((Q/b)^{4/3} y^{1/3} M^{2/3} / H_{\mathbf{b}}^{2/3},\, yQ/(2b))$. Combining the resulting bounds via Lemma LP395.16 leads to the three displayed conditions, the strongest being $\sigma > 1/18 + (28/9)\varpi + (2/9)\delta$, which implies the others.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition PrP395.10 (`lode')
nodes.statement: Reduce to the case $e=1$, $(\alpha l, m) = 1$. Apply Lemma LP395.12 (completion of sums in $n$); use Corollary CP395.3 (i) for the trivial regime and Corollary CP395.3 (ii) using $y$-dense divisibility of $m$ for the regime $m^{1/3} y^{1/3} \le \Delta \le m^{2/3} y^{-1/3}$. Extend to general $(\alpha l, m)$ by inclusion-exclusion mimicking Corollary CP395.1.

nodes.name: Complete the $n$-sum
nodes.statement: By Lemma LP395.12 (i), the sum over $n$ is bounded by $(N/m^{1/2} + m^{1/2}) \sup_h |\sum_d \psi_\Delta(d) K_h(d;m)|$ where $K_h(d;m) = m^{-1/2}\sum_n e_m(f(n,d) + hn)$.

nodes.name: Polya-Vinogradov + Deligne bound on the $d$-sum
nodes.statement: Apply Corollary CP395.3 (i) to obtain $|\sum_d \psi_\Delta(d) K_h(d;m)| \lessapprox m^{1/2} + \Delta m^{-1/2}$, giving the second bound (eq-lode-2) and the first bound for $\Delta > m^{2/3} y^{-1/3}$.

nodes.name: Trivial pointwise bound on $K_h$
nodes.statement: Use the pointwise bound $|K_h(d,m)| \lessapprox 1$ (CRT + (klo)) to handle the regime $\Delta \le m^{1/3} y^{1/3}$ giving the first bound there.

nodes.name: vdC step using $y$-dense divisibility
nodes.statement: In the regime $m^{1/3} y^{1/3} \le \Delta \le m^{2/3} y^{-1/3}$, factor $m = m_1 m_2$ with $m_i \sim m^{i/3} y^{(\pm)\cdot}$ and apply Corollary CP395.3 (ii) to get $|\sum_d \psi_\Delta(d) K_h(d;m)| \lessapprox \Delta^{1/2} m^{1/6} y^{1/6}$.

nodes.name: Inclusion-exclusion to remove $(\alpha l, m) > 1$
nodes.statement: Reduce general $\alpha, l$ to $(\alpha' l, m') = 1$ via $m' = m/(\alpha l, m)$, $y' = y(\alpha l, m)$, summing over $\delta \mid (\alpha l, m)$ via Mobius. Apply the previously proved case to each, then sum to obtain the full proposition.

nodes.name: Type IV/V extensions of the trichotomy
nodes.statement: For $1/14 < \sigma \le 1/10$ Lemma LP395.5 extends with Type IV and Type V cases, reflecting four or five powerful elements; however no profitable Type V estimate is available, blocking $\sigma < 1/10$ in this approach.

nodes.name: Iterated $q$-van der Corput
nodes.statement: Iterating the vdC argument across factorizations $q = r_1 \cdots r_l$ for $l \ge 3$ tends to be counterproductive in this paper, since the power of $q$ saved decays exponentially in $l$.

nodes.name: Type IV obstruction (higher convolutions)
nodes.statement: The Type III argument extended to fourth-order $\psi_1 \star \psi_2 \star \psi_3 \star \psi_4$ does not improve upon Bombieri-Vinogradov: with $H \approx Q^4/x \approx x$, neither diagonal $\approx x^{3/2}/S$ nor off-diagonal $\approx x^{3/2}/S^{5/2}$ can be made smaller than the target $x^{3/2}/S^2$.
